## Bayes Theorem & Conditional Probabilities Workshop

### Data

[Kaggle Stroke Prediction Dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/fedesoriano/stroke-prediction-dataset/data)

### Three Teams based on variable

1.  Gender
2.  Hypertension
3.  Heart Disease

### Exploratory Data Analysis

- Download the data
- Open an new QMD and name it conditional_probability_workshop
- Read the data in with `read_csv()` and `here()`
- Write R Code to create these 4 visualizations with `ggplot`

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

stroke <- read_csv(here("Data/healthcare-dataset-stroke-data.csv"))
glimpse(stroke)
```

```{r}
# Plotting copy of the data with readable labels (the original stroke data stays unchanged)
stroke_plot <- stroke %>%
  mutate(stroke_status = factor(stroke, levels = c(0, 1),
                                labels = c("No Stroke", "Stroke")))

stroke_colors <- c("No Stroke" = "#476EA0", "Stroke" = "#962323")
```

```{r}
# 1. Stroke count by gender
stroke_plot %>%
  filter(gender != "Other") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = gender, fill = stroke_status)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = stroke_colors) +
  labs(title = "Stroke Count by Gender", x = "Gender",
       y = "Number of Patients", fill = "Stroke Status") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```

```{r}
# 2. Age distribution by stroke status
ggplot(stroke_plot, aes(x = age, fill = stroke_status)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.5, color = "black", position = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = stroke_colors) +
  labs(title = "Age Distribution by Stroke Status", x = "Age",
       y = "Count", fill = "Stroke Status") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```

```{r}
# 3. Average glucose level by stroke status
ggplot(stroke_plot, aes(x = stroke_status, y = avg_glucose_level, fill = stroke_status)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = stroke_colors) +
  labs(title = "Average Glucose Level by Stroke Status", x = NULL,
       y = "Average Glucose Level") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
# 4. Stroke count by hypertension
stroke_plot %>%
  mutate(hypertension = factor(hypertension, levels = c(0, 1),
                               labels = c("No Hypertension", "Hypertension"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = hypertension, fill = stroke_status)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = stroke_colors) +
  labs(title = "Stroke Count by Hypertension", x = "Hypertension Status",
       y = "Number of Patients", fill = "Stroke Status") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```

```{r}
# 5. Stroke count by heart disease
stroke_plot %>%
  mutate(heart_disease = factor(heart_disease, levels = c(0, 1),
                                labels = c("No Heart Disease", "Heart Disease"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = heart_disease, fill = stroke_status)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = stroke_colors) +
  labs(title = "Stroke Count by Heart Disease", x = "Heart Disease Status",
       y = "Number of Patients", fill = "Stroke Status") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```

### Find the Conditional Probability of Stroke P(B\|A) based on

1.  Being a Male
2.  Having Hypertension
3.  Having Heart Disease

##### P(B): probability of stroke

```{r}
probability_stroke <- stroke %>%
  count(stroke) %>%
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) %>%
  filter(stroke == 1) %>%
  pull(percent)

probability_stroke
```

##### 1. Male

```{r}
# P(A|B): male given stroke
probability_male_given_stroke <- stroke %>%
  count(stroke, gender) %>%
  group_by(stroke) %>%
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) %>%
  filter(stroke == 1, gender == "Male") %>%
  pull(percent)

# P(A): male
probability_male <- stroke %>%
  count(gender) %>%
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) %>%
  filter(gender == "Male") %>%
  pull(percent)

# P(B|A): stroke given male
probability_male_given_stroke * probability_stroke / probability_male
```

##### 2. Hypertension

```{r}
probability_hypertension_given_stroke <- stroke %>%
  count(stroke, hypertension) %>%
  group_by(stroke) %>%
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) %>%
  filter(stroke == 1, hypertension == 1) %>%
  pull(percent)

probability_hypertension <- stroke %>%
  count(hypertension) %>%
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) %>%
  filter(hypertension == 1) %>%
  pull(percent)

probability_hypertension_given_stroke * probability_stroke / probability_hypertension
```

##### 3. Heart disease

```{r}
probability_heart_given_stroke <- stroke %>%
  count(stroke, heart_disease) %>%
  group_by(stroke) %>%
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) %>%
  filter(stroke == 1, heart_disease == 1) %>%
  pull(percent)

probability_heart <- stroke %>%
  count(heart_disease) %>%
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) %>%
  filter(heart_disease == 1) %>%
  pull(percent)

probability_heart_given_stroke * probability_stroke / probability_heart
```

### Report out your conditional probabilities and we will compare

Given a patient is male, there is about a 5.1% chance of stroke; given hypertension, about 13.3%; given heart disease, about 17.0%.

### Discussion

What question are we asking exactly - [WHO](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/stroke) - [Data Quality](https://link.springer.com/10.1186/s12916-026-04981-y)

We're estimating P(stroke \| male, hypertension, heart disease.
